name: Nephrology and kidney care
summary: How expats find kidney specialists for hypertension-related kidney disease, chronic kidney disease monitoring, dialysis planning, and transplant follow-up under Singapore hospital and private clinic pathways.
body:
Kidney care sits at the intersection of primary care, cardiology, and endocrine control of blood pressure and diabetes. Expats often arrive after a home-country diagnosis of chronic kidney disease (CKD), proteinuria, or recurrent kidney stones — or after a GP flags rising creatinine on a routine panel.

## What nephrologists manage
- CKD staging and slowing progression (blood pressure, glucose, ACE/ARB or newer agents as appropriate)
- Glomerular disease workup when urine protein or blood is unexplained
- Dialysis modality counselling (haemodialysis vs peritoneal) when eGFR declines
- Transplant evaluation and post-transplant immunosuppression follow-up for patients already grafted overseas
- Recurrent stones with metabolic workup beyond one-off urology lithotripsy

Urology remains the first stop for acute obstruction, stones needing intervention, and surgical kidney issues — nephrology owns medical kidney disease and long-term filtration decline.

## Public vs private
Public hospital nephrology (NUH, SGH, TTSH, CGH, KTPH and partners) runs multidisciplinary CKD clinics and dialysis units. Waiting times vary; bring prior labs, imaging, and medication lists. Private nephrologists at specialist centres and Gleneagles / Mount Elizabeth / Farrer Park / Parkway East clusters offer faster first visits and easier evening slots — useful when you need a second opinion before a home-country trip or before starting a pregnancy with known CKD.

Dialysis is a major cost and logistics decision. Confirm whether your Integrated Shield or international policy covers chronic dialysis and vascular access surgery before choosing a unit. Tourist or short-visit dialysis slots exist but must be booked early and are rarely identical to home-country machines or schedules.

## Medication and monitoring
Many CKD drugs are tightly dose-adjusted for eGFR. Keep a printed med list and latest labs when you travel. HSA rules still apply for controlled substances — see the medication import guide. Ask whether your nephrologist will share results with your overseas physician for continuous care.

## How to choose
Prefer board-certified nephrologists with clear CKD clinic pathways, dietitian access, and transparent dialysis affiliate relationships. Ask how they coordinate with cardiology and endocrinology when diabetes or heart failure coexists. For stone-heavy histories, confirm metabolic clinic follow-up rather than procedure-only care.

## Practical tip
Bring three months of labs (creatinine, eGFR, urine ACR, electrolytes) and blood-pressure logs to the first visit. If you are on transplant meds, carry the protocol letter — Singapore pharmacists may need specialist confirmation before dispensing certain immunosuppressants.
whenToEngage: Rising creatinine / eGFR trends after GP labs
Known CKD or transplant history needs Singapore follow-up
Recurrent stones need metabolic (not procedure-only) workup
Dialysis or pregnancy planning with reduced kidney function
